name: Goblet squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest. Stand at a slight angle to the camera so both knees are visible, with your whole body including feet in frame. Squat down under control, then stand back up.

cues.message: Try to sit a little lower — you are stopping above your usual depth
One knee is bending noticeably more than the other

knownLimitations: EXPERIMENTAL: no physical validation has been performed. Thresholds are engineering guesses, not measured values.
Depth is inferred from knee angle, not from hip-versus-knee height, so a very upright squat with long femurs may score differently from a coached 'parallel' call.
The asymmetry cue compares knee angles in the image plane. It is only meaningful in the front-diagonal view and abstains elsewhere.
Heel lift, knee valgus and spinal position are not measured at all. Silence from this exercise is not a statement that the squat was good.
unsupportedViews: SIDE: the far leg is occluded, so a bilateral knee angle cannot be measured and the asymmetry cue is meaningless.
FRONT (square on): knee flexion is heavily foreshortened; depth reads as shallower than it is.
